authoring_rules: Sixth held-out set, for the summarizer-candidate decision of CANDIDATE_V4.md (arms BASE, V2, V4).
Written from the source at the pinned commits before any engine, search, ranking or summarizer ran on these repositories. Only a name-only index (candidate pool names, check.py) was built.
Same rules as sets 1-5: developer phrasing; gold = the function(s) that directly answer; decoys = plausible wrong functions (same stems, the caller or the helper, a sibling).
No question contains its gold symbol's name or every word of it (check.py).
Gold and decoys are library code, never test files; no property setter (#2) is gold or decoy.

questions.question: When the client follows a 3xx to another host, which fields are stripped from the next outgoing request, and why does a plain http-to-https upgrade keep the credentials?
After a 302 or 303 response, when does the follow-up request switch from POST to GET, and why is HEAD left alone?
How is the Location value of a 3xx turned into the next address to visit, including relative paths and a missing host or fragment?
How are HTTP_PROXY, HTTPS_PROXY and NO_PROXY variables turned into mount patterns, and what does a wildcard in the bypass list do?
How does the library find out how many bytes an uploaded file object holds without reading it, falling back to seeking to the end?
When several mount patterns could match an address, how are they ordered so that ones with a port and longer hostnames win?
Where are credential-bearing fields like Authorization masked as [secure] when a request or its header collection is printed?
Which character set is used to decode raw header bytes, trying ascii, then utf-8, and finally latin-1?
Which quality-of-protection option is chosen from a digest challenge, and when does auth-int raise a not-implemented error?
How are dot and dot-dot segments removed from the route component of an address, following RFC 3986?
When streaming a body line by line, how are partial lines buffered across chunks and a trailing carriage return carried into the next piece?
How does a response pick how to decompress its body from the Content-Encoding values, chaining several when gzip and br are both listed?
How does a response throw an error on 4xx and 5xx codes, with a message naming the error class and the Location when it is a 3xx?
How does the library decide whether an outgoing body becomes raw bytes, a multipart form, a url-encoded form or JSON, and warn when bytes are passed as form data?
How are low-level connection-pool errors translated into the library's own exception types, picking the most specific match?
How is an integer total split into parts proportional to integer weights, honouring per-slot minimums so the parts add up exactly?
How does the terminal printer decide between truecolor, 256 and 16 colours from COLORTERM and TERM, and when does it turn colour off entirely?
How is a 24-bit RGB value reduced to the nearest index of the 256-colour cube, treating low-saturation values as grey?
How is the closest entry in a fixed colour table found for an RGB triple using a weighted redmean distance?
Given a byte count, how is the right power of 1000 or 1024 and its label like kB or MiB chosen?
How is user text made safe to embed among square-bracket style tags so it is not treated as formatting, including trailing backslashes?
How is the number of spaces per indent level of a code snippet worked out from the greatest common divisor of the even leading-space widths?
How are adjacent rendered pieces that share the same style merged into one to reduce the output written to the terminal?
How is a string broken into lines that each fit a given terminal column width when it contains double-width characters?
How is styled text shortened to a maximum width, adding an ellipsis character or padding with spaces when asked?
How is the rate of a running task in steps per second estimated from its recent samples?
How is the estimated time left for a task shown as h:mm:ss or a compact mm:ss, with dashes when it is unknown?
When printing an exception's stack frames, how is the highlighting language for each source file chosen, including files with no extension that start with a python shebang?
When a grid's columns are too wide for the screen, how are the widest wrappable columns shrunk step by step until everything fits?
How is a log record's severity name padded and styled before it is shown in the left column of the logging handler's output?
